title: How to Choose the Right LED Lighting for Commercial Spaces
excerpt: A practical guide to evaluating illumination levels, colour quality, efficiency, controls, and long-term operating cost for commercial projects.
author: Clair Lighting Team
seoTitle: How to Choose Commercial LED Lighting
seoDescription: Learn how to select efficient commercial LED lighting using illumination levels, colour quality, controls, maintenance, and lifecycle cost.

children.text: The right lighting system does more than make a space visible. It supports productivity, improves comfort, presents products accurately, and influences the total energy cost of a building.
Start with the activity, not the fixture

An office, retail floor, warehouse aisle, reception area, and meeting room all need different light distributions and illumination levels. Define the visual task, ceiling height, surface colours, operating hours, and daylight conditions before selecting wattage or form factor.
Evaluate light quality
Consider colour temperature, colour rendering index, glare control, flicker performance, and uniformity. A high lumen figure alone cannot guarantee a comfortable or effective environment.
Compare lifecycle cost

Compare efficacy, rated life, driver quality, warranty, maintenance access, and compatibility with occupancy or daylight controls. The lowest purchase price is rarely the lowest cost over the full life of a commercial installation.

title: Lumens, Wattage and Colour Temperature Explained
excerpt: Understand the three lighting specifications buyers encounter most often and how to use each one when comparing modern LED products.
author: Clair Lighting Team
seoDescription: A clear explanation of lumens, wattage and colour temperature, with practical guidance for comparing LED lighting products.

children.text: LED technology changed the way lighting products should be compared. Wattage is no longer a reliable shortcut for brightness, so buyers need to understand a few separate measurements.
Lumens measure light output
Lumens describe the quantity of visible light produced. Use delivered lumens and the fixture's optical distribution when judging whether a product can illuminate the intended area.
Wattage measures power consumption

Watts indicate electrical demand. Comparing lumens per watt helps show how efficiently products turn electricity into useful light, but efficiency should be considered alongside reliability and light quality.
Colour temperature shapes atmosphere
Measured in kelvin, lower colour temperatures appear warmer while higher values appear cooler. The best choice depends on the materials, activity, desired atmosphere, and surrounding daylight.

title: Why Energy-Efficient Lighting Is a Smart Business Investment
excerpt: Efficient lighting can reduce operating cost while improving visibility, maintenance planning, and control across commercial and industrial facilities.
author: Clair Lighting Team
seoDescription: Discover how efficient LED lighting can reduce energy and maintenance costs while improving control in business facilities.

children.text: Lighting often operates for long hours, making it a practical target for efficiency improvements. A well-planned upgrade can deliver benefits beyond a smaller electricity bill.
Lower connected load

Modern LED systems can deliver the required illumination using less power than older technologies. Controls can reduce consumption further by responding to occupancy, schedules, and available daylight.
More predictable maintenance

Long-life products reduce replacement frequency, access equipment, labour disruption, and spare inventory. Product quality and thermal management remain essential to achieving the expected service life.
Build the business case
Record existing wattage, operating hours, maintenance costs, and illumination levels. Compare those figures with the proposed design and verify the result through a pilot area before a large rollout.
